From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Roberts <alice@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Alice,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the deep dive with you and the Acme engineering team. I promised to capture a short recap of the call, the key pain points and goals we heard, and clear next steps so everyone is aligned.

Summary (what you told us):
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference latency spikes (tail latency up to ~800ms for 256-token requests) and CPU/GPU contention during peak batch loads.
- Business goals: 99th percentile latency <= 250ms for interactive UI flows, sustained throughput to handle 1,200 qps during peak batch ingest, and predictable per-token cost under $0.0008.
- Constraints: data residency in the US, desire for private VPC deployment behind your subnet, and SOC 2 evidence requirement for audit.

Technical requirements discussed:
- Target p95/p99 SLOs: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 250ms for 256-token generation workload (single-turn).
- Throughput target: 1,200 qps steady-state with burst capacity to 2,500 qps for 10m windows.
- Model family: preference for an open LLM (Llama-3 or equivalent); you indicated willingness to evaluate a distilled/quantized variant if quality holds.
- KV cache behavior: long chat sessions (avg 1,500 tokens) — need cache pinning and cold-start mitigation.
- Networking: strict egress rules, TLS mutual-auth for control plane, and VPC peering to your infra.

Proposed deployment topology (high level):
- Private Redwood Private deployment in your VPC (customer-managed control plane) with a Dedicated GPU pool for inference nodes.
- Model variants: 1) FP16 Llama-3 for highest quality in dedicated pool; 2) 8-bit quantized variant for cost-sensitive routes.
- Smart routing: low-latency routes for interactive traffic with aggressive prefix caching; batch ingestion routed to a cost-tier pool with autoscaling.

Attachments: I attached an SLO-template (SLO-template.xlsx) and a high-level Redwood architecture snapshot (redwood-arch.png) we referenced on the call.

Open questions / clarifications we need from Acme:
1) Can you share representative latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) for recent production traffic and a sample of requests (anonymized)?
2) For the 1,200 qps throughput target, is that single-region or multi-region?
3) Any constraints on allowed quantization (e.g., disallow 8-bit for certain models due to quality/regulatory issues)?

Next steps (agreed on call):
- Acme: share latency histograms and a sanitized sample set by EOD Monday (Alice).
- Redwood: produce a Dedicated capacity estimate and an initial topology diagram with expected p95/p99 projections (Connor & infra team) — ETA: 48 business hours.
- Joint: schedule a follow-up to review the capacity estimate and run a short projection test (10k synthetic requests) — propose Tue 2027-04-06 11:00 AM PT.

If anything above is inaccurate or missing, flag it and I will update. Otherwise we’ll proceed with Connor preparing the Dedicated topology and sizing estimate.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa/Alice — quick response after looking through their numbers and the network diagram. High level: this is feasible with Redwood Dedicated in their VPC. Key notes and assumptions below.

Sizing & topology (first-pass):
- Dedicated GPU pool: 12 x A100-80GB equivalent instances (split across 3 availability zones) for FP16 variant to meet p95/p99 targets for 256-token requests with prefix caching.
- Quantized pool: 8 x 4090-equivalent instances for the 8-bit routes (cost-optimized group).
- Autoscaling: scale-to-0 for cost tiers, scale-to-capacity with a +30% buffer for bursts (should meet 2,500 qps for 10m windows).
- KV cache: use persistent KV nodes with pinning for long sessions; estimate additional 2 x high-memory instances for cache durability.

Projected latency (based on current sample traces and our model perf):
- p50: ~85ms
- p95: ~140ms
- p99: ~230ms (within their target of <=250ms)

Infra blockers / action items:
1) VPC peering: Acme needs to allow peering and open specific control-plane ports; will require their networking to approve the peering request and egress rules.
2) KMS: we support customer-managed KMS — Acme will need to provision a key and grant Redwood principal access.
3) SOC 2 evidence: we can provide our SOC 2 report and audit artifacts — Marissa, I’ll flag security for the artifact list.

Attachments: dedicated-capacity-estimate.pdf (draft)

Next steps:
- Connor to share the draft capacity estimate (attached) and an architecture diagram for their review by EOD Mon.
- Marissa to collect the histograms and schedule Tue 4/6 sync to run projections.
